- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days — adjust for a downward bias in the middle to end of the forecast.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 88+), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, leading to overprediction in the immediate aftermath — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% after spikes.
- Mean reversion is strong in the last 5–7 days of the forecast — model often fails to reflect this, so apply a slight downward trend correction toward the end.
- Model underestimates when true price is trending downward — especially in the 10–20 day window — increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for lag.
- Forecast for day 1 is often too low — adjust upward by 1–3% to account for initial momentum or lag in model response.
- Model tends to ignore recent volatility — when history shows high variance, increase forecast volatility buffer (e.g., ±2–3% around mean) to reflect uncertainty.
